title: Jugal Hansraj Reunites With Shekhar Kapur for Masoom: The Next Generation
excerpt: The child star of the 1983 classic returns 43 years later, joining Naseeruddin Shah, Shabana Azmi, Manoj Bajpayee, and Nithya Menen in the spiritual sequel with A.R. Rahman composing the music.
body:
• Jugal Hansraj joins Masoom: The Next Generation, reuniting with director Shekhar Kapur and co-stars Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi after 43 years
  • The cast includes Manoj Bajpayee, Nithya Menen, and Kaveri Kapur, with A.R. Rahman composing music and co-producing
  • The spiritual sequel explores themes of family, identity, and what home means across generations

Actor Jugal Hansraj is returning to the Masoom universe more than four decades after he made his acting debut as a child in Shekhar Kapur's 1983 classic. Masoom: The Next Generation will reunite him with the original film's director and co-stars Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, according to Bollywood Hungama.

A Full-Circle Moment

Kapur described bringing Jugal back as deeply emotional. "There is something profoundly beautiful about coming home — not to a place, but to a story that has stayed alive in people's hearts for decades," the director said. "Jugal was just a young boy when we made Masoom, and today, welcoming him back as an accomplished actor is both emotional and deeply fulfilling. Reuniting him with Naseer and Shabana is a reminder that some relationships transcend cinema."

Jugal Hansraj, who still gets recognized as "the Masoom boy," said the decision to return was immediate. "When Shekhar called to tell me he wanted me to be a part of the new Masoom, it made me so happy. Masoom has been a part of my life, my identity, for as long as I can remember," he said.

"People still remember it with so much affection. I constantly get stopped by people even here in New York, and they tell me with a warm smile that their kids or grandkids still listen to 'Lakdi Ki Kathi.' It's like life coming full circle."

— Jugal Hansraj

The Cast and Crew

The ensemble brings together multiple generations of Indian cinema talent. Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, who played the parents in the original, will portray characters in their eighties. Manoj Bajpayee and Nithya Menen round out the senior cast, while Kapur's daughter Kaveri plays the daughter of an Indian father and an American mother.

Academy Award-winning composer A.R. Rahman is attached to compose the music and co-produce the film, a significant addition announced in May 2026. The original Masoom featured an iconic soundtrack by R.D. Burman with lyrics by Gulzar, including the timeless ghazal "Tujhse Naraz Nahin Zindagi" and the children's classic "Lakdi Ki Kathi."

Not a Direct Sequel

Masoom: The Next Generation is described as a spiritual sequel rather than a direct continuation of the 1983 story. Like the original — which was adapted from Erich Segal's 1980 novel Man, Woman and Child — the new film explores family relationships, identity, and changing dynamics across generations.

Kapur has said the film is rooted in the idea of home. "I started writing this film a decade ago, based on my experiences and my parents, who wanted to build a home in Delhi," he shared. The film will explore what home means — love, relationships, memories, and identities — as older parents navigate the reality of children who moved away and never came back.

Production Details

The film is set to be shot in Mumbai in a start-to-finish schedule. Kapur has emphasized that it is performance-driven, with weeks of workshops and rehearsals planned before cameras roll. "I don't want to push my actors. I want to give them space to discover the film and their characters," he said.

Kapur first announced the sequel at the International Film Festival Delhi (IFFD) 2026 in March. The original Masoom swept the 1984 Filmfare Awards, winning Best Film (Critics), Best Actor for Naseeruddin Shah, and Best Music Director for R.D. Burman.
